title: Orchestrated preflight capacity priming and acceptance quorum for cross-region failover
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Implement an orchestrated preflight sequence that brings a target cold/idle region into an operational state before re-routing live traffic. Goals: reduce failed cutovers, limit cold-start token/time penalty, and ensure model-variant compatibility. Key components: 1) capacity priming (spin warm allocator + synthetic micro-loads), 2) KV and prefix cache seeding for high-frequency keysets, 3) model-variant compatibility shim that verifies op kernel/quantization parity, 4) acceptance quorum scoring and circuit-breaker gating that require sustained healthy probes before traffic is shifted, and 5) cost-aware throttles to prevent excessive burst spending. This ticket builds the orchestration controller, probe types, and runbook hooks for operator intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule a preflight for a target region and report a progress timeline
Preflight performs KV/prefix cache seeding for configured keysets and reports hit-rate improvement > 20% under synthetic micro-load
Model-variant compatibility checks validate tokenizer, embedding dims, and kernel/quantization compatibility; incompatibilities surface as actionable errors
Acceptance quorum: at least 3/4 region-level probes (latency, kv-hit-rate, model-inference-correctness, memory pressure) must be green for a rolling 5m window before any percent-of-traffic is shifted
Circuit-breaker auto-abort and immediate rollback to origin if error-rate > 2% or p95 latency regresses by >30% within first 10 minutes
Observable metrics and dashboard panel available in Console with token-level cost estimate for the preflight run

notes: Trade-offs considered: pre-warming reduces user-visible latency but increases short-term cost; default preflight runs will be conservative (shorter duration, smaller pool sizes) for low-tier customers. For enterprise Dedicated tenants we allow configurable aggressive priming. We chose a quorum-based acceptance (N-of-M probes) to avoid single-point probe flakiness. Compatibility shim is intentionally strict: any mismatch forces fallback to a verified variant to preserve correctness. Operator flow: abort early on resource pressure; allow manual override with explicit risk acknowledgement.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Probe harness and model-variant compatibility shim (2w)
Phase 2: KV/prefix seeding API and seed-job templates (1w)
Phase 3: Orchestration controller, acceptance-quorum logic and circuit-breaker (2w)
Phase 4: Console integration and runbook + chaos engineering validation (1w)
risks: Short-term cost spikes from aggressive warmups
False positives/negatives in probes causing unnecessary rollbacks or unsafe promotions
Kernel/quantization mismatches leading to subtle model output regressions
Race conditions when simultaneously priming multiple regions for different tenants
